findings.text: factors that appear crowded on our model had a much higher frequency (over seven times higher) of significant drawdowns in factor performance over the subsequent 12 months
findings.evidence: We also find that factors that appear crowded on our model had a much higher frequency (over seven times higher) of significant drawdowns in factor performance over the subsequent 12 months than factors that did not appear crowded.

findings.text: the frequency of a 5% or larger drawdown in factor return in the next year is approximately 23% when the crowding score is above 1 — 7.5 times the frequency of 3% when the score is less than 0.5
findings.evidence: We see in Exhibit 7 that the frequency of a 5% or larger drawdown in factor return in the next year is approximately 23% when the crowding score is above 1 — 7.5 times the frequency of 3% when the score is less than 0.5.

findings.text: The peak correlation with future factor returns and volatility generally occurred at the 7-12 month horizon, indicating that crowding continued to build for some time before a reversal occurred
findings.evidence: The peak correlation with future factor returns and volatility generally occurred at the 7-12 month horizon, indicating that crowding continued to build for some time before a reversal occurred.

findings.text: high levels of crowding in a factor have historically implied greater risk of poor performance and higher volatility for that factor thereafter, particularly over the subsequent six to 12 months
findings.evidence: While not indicative of future events, we found that high levels of crowding in a factor have historically implied greater risk of poor performance and higher volatility for that factor thereafter, particularly over the subsequent six to 12 months.

findings.text: the integrated crowding score dropped several months before the momentum factor crashed suggests that the momentum crash of 2009 was not driven by crowding
findings.evidence: However, the fact that the integrated crowding score dropped several months before the momentum factor crashed suggests that the momentum crash of 2009 was not driven by crowding.
